outer_multicall_in_progress.meaning: an outer multicall batch operation is in progress
outer_multicall_in_progress.checkpoint: before the outer multicall loop processes the subsequent fee-requiring call

inner_call_is_nested_multicall.meaning: one inner call of the outer multicall is a delegatecall to multicall itself
inner_call_is_nested_multicall.checkpoint: before the nested inner multicall executes

subsequent_call_requires_fee.meaning: a subsequent call in the outer multicall requires a nonzero fee specified in its call parameters
subsequent_call_requires_fee.checkpoint: before the subsequent fee-requiring call executes

legitimate_batch_completes.meaning: the legitimate batch transaction that requires a fee completes successfully rather than failing
legitimate_batch_completes.checkpoint: after the outer multicall finishes processing the fee-requiring call

multicall_denied_service.meaning: the multicall functionality is denied service, i.e. the legitimate fee-requiring batch transaction fails
multicall_denied_service.checkpoint: after the outer multicall processes the subsequent fee-requiring call

assumptions: The nested multicall and the subsequent fee-requiring call occur within the same outer multicall transaction.
The legitimate batch transaction is the one containing the subsequent fee-requiring call.
The attacker crafts the nested multicall within the same transaction; no prior historical state is required.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the attacker must be authorized to call multicall or whether anyone can call it; the applicability scope of the DoS is therefore not fully determined.
Report does not specify the exact fee amount or the msg.value/msgValue comparison operands beyond msg.value == msgValue.

limitations: The impact is formalized as the potential failure of a legitimate fee-requiring batch transaction following a nested multicall; the report's 'potential' modality is preserved by treating the failure as the forbidden outcome under the crafted scenario rather than an inevitable effect.
The exact revert mechanism and fee comparison operands are not numerically bound; the plan uses report-grounded Boolean observables for the fee requirement and completion outcome.
Other impacts (e.g. breaks_core_feature) are not formalized in this plan.
